To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) genetic effects on production traits change over time; 2) genetic correlations between production and some fertility traits are negative; and 3), when genetic correlations were estimated within genotypes, the negative correlations were on average weaker for genotypes with the allele increasing the production.

1) genetic effects of milk production and fertility traits change over time; 2) the DGAT1 region contains many haplotype blocks with significant SNPs; 3) negative genetic correlations were found in general between yield and fertility; and 4) correlations were weaker between yield and fertility when the yield increasing SNP allele was present.

1) the genetic effects of SNPs on milk yield, milk fat, protein and somatic cell count change over time; 2) these effects can be separated into three different groups according to their dynamics; and 3), genetic correlations become stronger with progressing lactations and are generally negative between production and fertility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis for the dynamic expression of effects during the first 60 days in milk.
the genetic architecture of early lactation and the dynamics of the genetic effects on milk production and fertility traits.

the dynamics of genetic effects on milk production and fertility and the correlations between the traits during early lactation in Holstein Fiesian bulls, which is a prerequisite for further studies on the molecular basis of these traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic architecture of milk production and fertility traits is complex.
the genetic architecture of the production and fertility traits is more complex than previously assumed.
genetic effects are dynamic over time and that genetic correlations between production and reproductive traits depend on the lactation stage as well as on the genotype of an individual animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genetic effects on milk production and fertility traits are highly dependent on the lactation stage and that there is no evidence for antagonism between production and fertility in the early lactation stage.
milk yield in early lactation is not a good indicator for fertility in Holstein Fiesians.
there is no clear evidence for the existence of a tradeoff between milk production and fertility in Holstein Fiesians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture of production and fertility traits is complex, but that there are still possibilities for improving both traits simultaneously by selection of the right marker alleles.
the expression of effects on milk production and fertility traits during the first 60 days of lactation is not constant, but changes over time.
genetic correlations between production and health traits are highly dependent on the lactation stage.
